analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: three rows are added at head lines 1756-1758 to the env-var table (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS). They name source files (GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift) that are not in the supplied diff, so the implementation is unverified here. I examined the base text of the units and the patch, and the change is documentation only, with no executable code, config default, authorization, attestation, encryption, or billing path changed. The table sits in the 'Variable | Read by' list under the passthrough section, which says 'darkbloom start copies only these variables'. The new rows do not say whether these three are forwarded into the LaunchAgent plist. I did not treat that as a finding because this is a documentation ambiguity with no evidence of a security regression. Threat-model relevance is limited: T-041 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle, residual KV data, T-028) and TB-007 could be affected if the backing code changes segment retention, host zeroing, or the idle cache sweep, for example by retaining KV data longer, skipping zeroing, or altering the cache-sweep timing channel. The referenced Swift source and its default behavior were not supplied, so those effects cannot be assessed from this PR. The next pass should check, if the code ships elsewhere, that these TTFT knobs do not widen KV residual-data exposure (T-028), alter the SEC-035 timing oracle, or add undocumented persistence. No findings.
